copies.headline: Noah's Backfield Can't Outrun John's Tight Ends
copies.body:
John wins this at the positions Noah can't fix. Brock Bowers and Trey McBride is an unfair tight end room in a one-TE league — one of them is a WR2 riding the bench while Noah trots out Colston Loveland and prays a rookie tight end saves his week. Add Puka Nacua, who alone outprojects any receiver Noah owns, and John's ceiling is somewhere Noah's roster physically cannot reach. Stafford or Caleb Williams at quarterback is a nice problem; Drake Maye and nothing behind him is not.
Noah's case is De'Von Achane and James Cook chewing up 33 points against a Rams backfield that's Kyren Williams and a Blake Corum handcuff nobody wanted. That's real. But past those two it's Rhamondre Stevenson, Tyjae Spears, and a receiver corps of Mike Evans in San Francisco and three guys projected at ten. John by eleven, and it should feel worse than that.

copies.headline: Isaac Brought Receivers to a Backfield Fight
copies.body:
Isaac's roster is a wideout hoarding problem with a football team attached. Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, Terry McLaurin, DK Metcalf — seven guys who all want the same three slots, and behind them a backfield of Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo and Jaylen Warren that adds up to one mediocre RB1. Bo Nix at quarterback is a decision, not a plan, and the Malik Willis contingency plan is somehow worse. Hockenson or Kincaid at tight end is picking which nine-point coin flip you trust.
Kaleb wins this on the ground and at the top. Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall out-project Isaac's entire committee by seven, Justin Herbert clears Nix by three, and Harold Fannin Jr. is a real tight end. The soft spot is receiver — Drake London and Ladd McConkey are fine, then it drops off a cliff into Keenan Allen and rookie dart throws, and that Vikings defense projects for four points, which is basically a bye week. Kaleb by a nose.

copies.headline: Grant's Receivers Bury CJ's Running Back Hoard
copies.body:
CJ drafted like the waiver wire was going to be nuked from orbit — nine running backs, and the only ones that matter are Jonathan Taylor and whichever Browns body Quinshon Judkins is sharing a backfield with. Zach Charbonnet projects a literal zero. Meanwhile the receiver room is Rashee Rice, Emeka Egbuka, and then a cliff into Parker Washington and Alec Pierce, two guys who need a 60-yard bomb to be relevant. Jake Ferguson at tight end is fine in the way a gas station sandwich is fine.
Grant wins this on the flanks. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Zay Flowers, Jaylen Waddle, plus Christian Watson and Chris Godwin as spare parts — that's a six-point weekly edge before anyone gets cute. His problem is quarterback, where Kyler Murray and Baker Mayfield both project 16 and both can hand you nine. Burrow's the better arm. He's also the only reason CJ's in this. Grant by four, and it isn't as close as that.

copies.headline: Logan's Eagles Stack Meets Adam's Committee Casserole
copies.body:
Take Logan. He's got the only real ceiling in this game: Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley, the same offense, the same goal line, and Justin Jefferson stapled on top. Adam counters with a running back room that's four guys splitting three carries — Kenneth Walker III in Kansas City, Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell sharing Tampa, Rico Dowdle vulturing in Pittsburgh. That's not depth, that's a group project. Jayden Daniels is fine, but fine loses to Hurts by four before anyone tackles anybody.
Adam's actual edge is receiver, and it's thin — Jaxon Smith-Njigba is legit, Chris Olave has hamstrings made of tissue paper, and Rome Odunze needs Chicago to remember he exists. Two points at wideout and two at tight end won't cover seven at running back. Logan's one hole is Isaiah Likely alone at tight end, which matters if Adam gets vintage Mark Andrews. He won't. Logan by nine.

copies.headline: Christian's Tight End Room Is A Crime Scene
copies.body:
Christian wins the receiver room by a mile — CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith is a real one-two, and Jameson Williams and Khalil Shakir give him outs if Deebo keeps looking like a fullback. The problem is the tight end drawer: Chig Okonkwo for seven and a George Kittle who projects at literally zero, which means Christian's entire edge evaporates the second Peter starts Tucker Kraft and Lamar Jackson and just quietly banks four points at two spots. Chase Brown and Travis Etienne are fine. Fine doesn't cover a zero.
Peter's roster is the one with an actual foundation — Bijan Robinson, Lamar, Kraft — but look past the top and it's Jonathon Brooks and Kyle Monangai at ten apiece, which is how you lose a game by three. Peter's receivers are three good names and then Denzel Boston, Jalen McMillan and Jalen Nailor, a bye-week nightmare in waiting. Two-point spread, one Kittle donut. Peter takes it.

copies.headline: Leif Hoards Quarterbacks, Loses Everywhere Else
copies.body:
Leif has Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes on the same roster, which is a great way to win one lineup spot by a single point and lose the other three. Behind the QB vanity project, the receiving room is Davante Adams at 33, Marvin Harrison Jr. still waiting on a quarterback who can find him, and Jayden Reed splitting targets in Green Bay's committee. The tight end plan is Kyle Pitts, a man who has been a breakout candidate for five straight years and delivered nothing. Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry are real, but Henry's 32 and the depth behind them is Woody Marks and a guy named Kaelon Black.
Mitchell isn't clean either — starting Jaxson Dart in Week 1 is a choice, and Alvin Kamara projecting zero is roster rot. But Jahmyr Gibbs and Josh Jacobs beat Leif's backfield, Nico Collins and Courtland Sutton beat his wideouts, and Tyler Warren beats Pitts by simply being younger. Mitchell by six, and it should be more.

intro: Isaac at Kaleb is the only game the projections can't separate — 118.6 to 120.7, two points, which means it'll come down to whichever tight end remembers he plays football. Meanwhile Noah gets shipped to John down ten, and Christian opens with the lowest projected total on the board, which is a rough way to find out your draft was a group project you did alone. Adam at Logan and Leif at Mitchell both look like scheduled beatings; the only question is whether the losers admit it before Sunday night or after.
